header: WHAT A STORY'S OWN PAGE SAYS: ITS PICTURE, AND WHETHER IT IS FREE TO READ. The owner's rules: a story with no picture is not shown, and a story that needs a subscription is not shown. Both are read from the story's page while a tab is being built. THE PICTURE is the one the paper attaches (its og:image, what a link preview shows), taken from the page's <meta> tags. PAID is what the paper itself says, in the way papers tell search engines about a paywall: the page's structured data (JSON-LD) says `"isAccessibleForFree": false` (or "False"). Seen on 28 Nov 2026: The Hindu says it of every story I read, Mint and The Hindu BusinessLine of their premium ones only, Hindustan Times, Indian Express, NDTV and Times of India say true or nothing. A page that answers 401 or 402 (The Wall Street Journal's does) wants a login, so it is paid; an address that says it is a premium section (/premium/, /prime/, /subscriber) is paid. A paper that says nothing is taken as free: the card says so, because that is not a check but the absence of a mark. A page that could not be read (403, a timeout) is UNKNOWN, not paid. Only a bounded amount of each page is read (400 KB, and not past the point where both the head has ended and the marker has been seen), the newest stories only, a few at a time, within a deadline, and every answer is kept (a day when read; five minutes when not), so that after the first build only the stories that have just appeared cost a request. Only the papers whose pages answer an ordinary request are read (ARTICLE_HOSTS in thumb.ts); one that refuses (Anandabazar Patrika, The Telegraph) is not worked around.

members.name: image
doc: The picture the paper attaches to the story (an https address on an allowed image server), or null.

members.name: paid
doc: True when the paper marks the story as needing a subscription (or the page wants a login); false when it says free or says nothing.

members.name: read
doc: False when the page could not be read (the answer is then a guess to be asked again soon).

behaviours: a page whose structured data says isAccessibleForFree false is paid: false (The Hindu), "False" (Mint), and either of two entries being false
true, "True" or no mark at all is not paid (free, or nothing said: the card says that a missing mark is not a check)
an address that names a premium section is paid (its path, not its host): /premium/, /prime/, /subscriber-only/; an ordinary address and a host called premium are not
the facts of a page: its picture (og:image on an allowed server) and its paid mark together
a page is read until the head has ended AND the mark has been seen (Mint's is far down the page, past the head), and not to its end
a paper that puts no mark is read only to 150 KB past its head, never to the end of a megabyte page
a free story gives its picture and is not paid
a page that answers 401 or 402 (The Wall Street Journal's does) wants a login: paid
a page that refuses (403) or fails is UNKNOWN, neither paid nor free: not read
a paper whose pages are not read (Anandabazar Patrika, The Telegraph, a Google link) is never fetched
a redirect that leaves the papers' hosts is not followed into
the facts of several stories are had together; links of papers that are not read are left out
what has been read is kept: asking again costs no request
a deadline stops the looking: with 40 slow pages, 5 at a time and 400 ms, only a part is read, and the answer comes at about the deadline, not after all of them
